newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices continue retreat on weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices continue retreat on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were sharply lower again on Tuesday as mild temperatures in the central U.S. headed eastward and next week's forecasts called for more above-normal temperatures, sources said.
Prices on the Gulf Coast pipes fell another 25 cents to the $2.90s amid ample storage supplies in the East and lingering mild temperatures in the Midwest.
In south Texas, prices softened by about 10 cents to the mid-$2.80s, down about a $1 from January indices, as temperatures remained near to slightly above-normal in the region.
In the Midcontinent, prices were steady to slightly weaker in the $2.80s.
Giving some support to the cash market is the forecast for another cold front in the Midwest by Thursday or Friday, dragging temperatures to about four to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal.
Chicago city-gate values were talked about five to 10 cents lower in the $3.15-3.20 range.
In west Texas, Permian prices held steady in the $2.74-2.83 range. Waha deals were reported done mostly around $2.80.
However, prices at the southern California border fell by about 30 cents to the mid-to-high $2.70s. The main culprit, traders said, was the seasonably mild weather now in the Southwest.
In the East, where stocks are well above year-ago levels and temperatures are rising, prices drifted into the $3.50-3.80 range, down at least 20 cents from Monday.
